title: Platform feature-flag store, its schema name and the deployment of the admin component are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-047 section 13 (Database, Flyway migration V2026_11_47__p2_feature_flags.sql); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 29; Ownership Map v1 (feature_flag and feature_flag_change owned by PLT)
description: No source names the platform-owned store that holds feature_flag and feature_flag_change, the schema name that store uses, or where the admin component of the library is deployed. Architecture v5 slide 29 fixes one schema and one login per service for the 19 services and names no platform schema, and the Ownership Map keeps the two tables with PLT without naming a store.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and the shared libraries) and slide 29 (19 Recovery schemas rwb_<service>, one login each); Ownership Map ruling on feature_flag: feature flags stay with the platform library and P2 serves the admin API against the library; no slide and no technical specification names the feature-flag store or its schema.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) architect with the ACE DBA
proposed: Create one platform-owned store with a schema name allocated by RWB-PLT-DB, let the library cache per service, and deploy the admin component with the rwb-integration platform route; record the allocation before the store migration is written.

title: Feature-flag contract schemas, the schema names of the two PLT tables and the idempotency rule of the POST are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-047 section 12 (Contract table and the Idempotency column); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11; Ownership Map v1
description: No technical specification defines the published feature-flag schemas, the schema names of feature_flag and feature_flag_change, or the report input and output. The legacy contract states uniqueness for the POST and names no Idempotency-Key header, while Architecture v5 slide 11 requires an Idempotency-Key on every POST and errors as RFC 9457 problem details.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-047 section 12 (POST returns 409 when the key exists; PATCH uses If-Match with the version); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST, RFC 9457 problem details, one hop, 2 s timeout); Ownership Map ruling on feature_flag; no technical specification exists for the platform library.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) contract owner with the ACE DBA
proposed: Publish the schemas from the legacy field identifiers DF-OPS-207 to DF-OPS-223 and the standard columns, keep the schema names as the placeholder until RWB-PLT-DB allocates them, and publish the POST with an Idempotency-Key and the PATCH with If-Match.

title: The rule-model fetch has no Ownership Map row, the shape of the fetched model is not specified, the RulePackageInForce subscriber list covers only four services, and the package format of phase 1 rests on a proposal
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 14, 20, 27, 28, 29, 41, 43 and 44); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 12, 14, 15 and 16); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owner P7, ASM-A6-tables-3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 072 Drools runtime and rule package store v1.md (sections 3, 4, 5, 11, 12 and 13)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 13 Solution plan
description: (a) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 27 and Temporal and Drools design slide 15 name GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} as the model fetch that an owning service calls, but the Ownership Map and the API Specification hold no path and no owner for it: the DMN model registry is P7 and the fetch operation itself is unowned. (b) No source states the shape of what the fetch returns. The legacy story read drl_source, checksum, valid_from and valid_to from rule_package_version and the catalog fields from rule_row in one database, and the Temporal and Drools design slide 15 keeps a workbook, a generated DRL and a SHA-256 per version, but nothing says whether the fetch carries the DRL, a compiled artefact or both, how the ordered rows and their catalog projection travel, or which error codes a refused fetch returns. (c) Architecture v5 slide 43 lists rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment as the consumers of RulePackageInForce, while DP-04 embeds the kit in every service and 14 of the 19 services own a package, so the subscriber list for the other services is not stated. (d) The phase-1 package format is a proposal and not a decision in the source set: Architecture v5 slide 27 states that XLS decision tables are Drools-native and compile to DRL and that OMG DMN 1.6 is the later target on the same runtime, without dating the move. The kit's loader, cache and contract fake cannot be specified from the sources without (b) at least, and the story cannot say which services subscribe without (c).
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 rwb-decision IN: REST POST /rule-models and GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, and EVT RulePackageInForce; slide 27 RUN IN THE OWNING SERVICE: Load GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}, verify checksum, swap in; Evaluate inside an activity, under 300 ms; Record answer and model version in the decision record, with the note that governance stays central in rwb-decision and evaluation is local; slide 43 row 30 RulePackageInForce, producer rwb-decision, topic rwb.decision.events.v1, consumers rwb-case, rwb-valuation, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment; slide 41 P7 owns approvals, central decision ledger and DMN model registry in schema rwb_decision; Temporal and Drools design slide 11 each service packages the embedded Drools runtime, and the owning service loads a version on RulePackageInForce, verifies the checksum, swaps atomically and keeps the last good model, cache max 20; slide 15 WHAT IS STORED FOR EVERY VERSION rule_package_version: workbook in Blob, generated DRL, SHA-256, valid-from date, approver, with the note that XLS tables are compiled to DRL and DMN 1.6 is the target; slide 16 KieBaseRegistry holds one KieBase per package version, LRU, max 20; Ownership Map rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owner P7 with ASM-A6-tables-3 and no api row for the fetch; RWB-E1-072 section 12 published the interfaces and one endpoint, and section 13 read the store from rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_row directly.
proposed: Publish the fetch on rwb-decision as one response carrying the package code, the version label, the checksum, the ordered rows of the version and the catalog projection of each row; name rwb-decision as the owner of the operation; and have every service that holds a model subscribe to RulePackageInForce on rwb.decision.events.v1 through its own inbox. Record the phase-1 format as the XLS decision table compiled to DRL with DMN 1.6 as the later target, and keep 20 as the cache default read through the parameters contract.

title: The kit contract has no source for its artefact coordinates, for the error codes of a refused model fetch, and for the message prefix of a refusal that now belongs to rwb-decision
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 20, 27 and 41); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md (slides 11, 14, 15 and 28); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (api rows and rule_* owners P7); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 072 Drools runtime and rule package store v1.md (sections 12, 13 and 14)
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: (a) No source states the coordinates under which the embedded rules kit is published as a library — the group, the artefact name and the release cadence — although every service depends on it and the platform baseline is the only place such naming could come from. (b) No source gives the error content of a refused or failed model fetch: the legacy story mapped every refusal to MSG-P3-027 with a {check} and a {detail}, but the HTTP status codes, the problem type and the message catalogue of the fetch on rwb-decision are not stated anywhere, so the contract can publish the refusal of the kit's own exception and not the transport errors of the fetch. (c) The refusal keeps the identifier MSG-P3-027, whose P3 prefix names rwb-case, while the store, the governance and therefore the refusal now sit with rwb-decision (P7); no source renumbers it, and no source publishes the rwb-decision message catalogue. The contract's rule that the identifier is kept unchanged, its non-retryable classification and its placeholder text are therefore a default of this run rather than a sourced value.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 REST: OpenAPI 3.1, /v1 in the path, RFC 9457 problem details, one hop and a 2 s timeout, with no message catalogue; slide 20 every service from the service template and shared libraries, naming the libraries but not their coordinates; slide 27 the load step verifies the checksum and swaps in while the note leaves governance central in rwb-decision; slide 41 P7 owns approvals, central decision ledger and DMN model registry; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 each owning service fetches the model, verifies the checksum and swaps it in, and rollback is one call; slide 28 a new rule version that is faulty is refused at load and the current version keeps running, with no error code; RWB-E1-072 section 12 published the interfaces and one package list endpoint with 401, 403, 404 and 503, and section 14 carried MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P4-002 only; Ownership Map rule_package and rule_package_version owner P7 with ASM-A6-tables-3 and no api row for GET /rule-models/{n}/{v}.
proposed: Take the artefact coordinates from the platform library baseline and record them on the contract at the version freeze; publish the fetch errors from rwb-decision's own document when it exists; and keep MSG-P3-027 unchanged, non-retryable, with the legacy text restored when the message catalogue is confirmed.

title: The retry schedule, the JOB-11 sender and the ownership of the exception path are unresolved for the outbox library
source: Legacy story RWB-TE-006 sections 3, 4, 5, 12 and 13; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 21, 22, 34, 41 and 44; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 28; Template and Rules v1 sections R3 and R5.5 (DP-09, DP-10)
section: Preconditions; Exception paths; Business rules; State transitions; Contract 12.3 to 12.9; Solution plan
description: Three legacy decisions are changed by the target architecture or left open. One, the retry schedule: the legacy settings are 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes after the previous attempt, while Architecture v5 slides 11 and 22 fix the Kafka retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and then the dead-letter topic with an alert and a replay tool. Two, the sender: the legacy sender is the clustered Quartz job JOB-11 running every minute over due rows of one recovery schema table, while Architecture v5 slide 44 maps JOB-11 to the owner every service with the mechanism outbox relay to Kafka and no Temporal Schedule, and slide 20 gives every service a continuous outbox relay. Three, the exception path: the legacy story sets a delivery to EXCEPTION, raises task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY and raises RETRY_LIMIT_REACHED with a decision log entry in one transaction inside one module, while in the target the case-step events, the task and the decision record belong to the service that owns the case step and cannot be raised by a shared library, and the dead-letter path belongs to Kafka and the platform team. The sources do not state which part of that exception path the library performs and which part the consumer owner service performs, nor which retry windows a test must use on Day 1.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-006 section 3 (retry settings 3 retries at 1, 5 and 15 minutes; Quartz clustered, JOB-11 every minute), section 4 steps 4 to 8, section 5 X10, section 12 job rows, section 13 build steps 4 to 7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 call-type table (retry topics 1 min / 10 min / 1 h, then .dlt + alert; inbox dedupe), slide 20 notes (Every service: built from one template with outbox relay), slide 21 notes (ordering by caseId), slide 22 notes (retry topics and dead-letter topic with an alert and a replay tool), slide 34 notes (Kafka down: events wait in each service outbox), slide 44 row JOB-11 (owner every service, mechanism outbox relay to Kafka); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 28 notes (failed messages go to retry topics then the dead-letter topic with an alert); Ownership Map jobs JOB-11 (owner PLT, replacement: no Temporal Schedule, outbox relay to Kafka in every service)
proposed: Apply R-PREC: keep the legacy values only in the preserved criteria text and adopt the Kafka retry ladder of 1 min, 10 min and 1 h plus the dead-letter topic; make the relay a continuous per-service worker that replaces the Quartz JOB-11 sender and is not a Temporal Schedule; and fix in the contract of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON which part of the exception path the library owns and which part the owning service of the case step owns, with one alert to the platform administrator on the dead-letter path.

title: The library contract shape, its publication channel and the split of the retry and exception path are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-TE-006 section 12 (published interfaces, job and the two admin endpoints); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 22, 29 and 44; Template and Rules v1 sections R3 and R5.5 (DP-01, DP-09, DP-15); Ownership Map tables outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, idempotency_key and jobs JOB-11
section: Preconditions; Exception paths; State transitions; Data; Contract 12.3 to 12.9; Solution plan
description: The legacy story publishes two interfaces and one consumer interface inside one module, with the writer and the consumer in the same recovery schema, and it gives the two outbox tables only. The target needs a contract that 19 services consume: the artifact name, the version scheme and the publication channel of the platform library are not stated anywhere; the column set of the inbox table processed_event and of the idempotency_key table is not given (the legacy story names them without a definition and the design of RWB-E1-007 is behind another contract); the event-type naming with the schema version in ce_type is fixed only by example on slide 22; and the retry and exception split of the contract is not stated. Two further conflicts are carried by the same row: the legacy retry settings of 1, 5 and 15 minutes against the Kafka ladder of 1 min, 10 min and 1 h of slide 22, and the case-step effects of task and case event which the target gives to the owning service rather than to the library.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-006 section 12 (UUID OutboxWriter.publish, ConsumeResult OutboxConsumer.consume, boolean IdempotencyGuard.firstTime, the two admin endpoints, the job table) and section 13 (outbox_event and outbox_delivery DDL only); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 call-type table (AsyncAPI 3.0, JSON Schema registry backward compatible, retry topics 1 min / 10 min / 1 h then .dlt + alert, inbox dedupe), slide 20 notes (every service from the service template and shared libraries; own schema with outbox and inbox), slide 22 (CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode, ce_id, ce_type rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1, ce_source, ce_subject, traceparent, key caseId; processed_event in each consumer), slide 29 notes (one schema and one login per service, Flyway per service, no cross-schema keys), slide 44 row JOB-11 (owner every service, outbox relay to Kafka); Ownership Map tables (outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, idempotency_key owner PLT, library objects created in every service schema)
proposed: Fix the contract in RWB-PLT-TE006-CON: one published artifact with a major version, the three interfaces with their exceptions, the DDL template of the four tables including the processed_event and idempotency_key columns, the CloudEvents 1.0 attribute set with the caseId key and the ce_type shape, the inbox dedupe rule, the retry ladder of 1 min, 10 min and 1 h plus the dead-letter topic with one alert and the replay tool, and the statement that the case-step events, the task and the decision record stay with the owning service.

title: The baseline package registry, module list, baseline version and release artefacts are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 section R7.2 s12 and R9; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 6, 11, 20, 22, 35, 38 and 49; legacy NF-02 description
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 12.8 Contract fakes; 12.9 Call-type summary; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: No source read fixes the package registry and its coordinates, the package and module names, the module split inside each of the five areas, the baseline version number and its versioning scheme, the retention of a superseded version, the exact contents of the software bill of materials and the checksum, the changelog format, the set of usage examples, the pin mechanism in the service template and the exact text of the drift, publish-gate and redaction messages.
evidence: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 38 state only that every service comes from the service template and the shared libraries and that wave 0 builds the template once; slides 6, 11, 22, 35 and 49 fix the trace, error, authorisation and no-personal-data standards but no registry, package, version or artefact detail; the legacy key gives the area list and the instruction to publish with versioning and examples, and no value beyond it.
proposed: Publish the registry coordinates, the module list per area, the baseline version and its versioning scheme, the release artefact set (source, bill of materials, checksum, changelog, usage example), the superseded-version retention, the pin mechanism in the service template and the message text, at the wave 0 platform review before the first consuming service is generated.
